headline: A preprint reports distributed agents scaling interpretation of a whole-brain perturbation atlas
summary: A bioRxiv preprint and Oct 21 OpenAI research report describe distributed biological reasoning: thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents separately analyzed perturbations in an existing whole-brain Perturb-seq atlas and combined results into a reasoning atlas. The authors report completing analysis in 32 minutes, citing over 700 references versus 11 in a largest-workload single-agent comparison, and blinded experts preferring distributed reports 75% of the time. A DCTN1/cholesterol relationship is presented as a hypothesis for follow-up experiments. These are author-reported results from one dataset; the reported biology is not experimentally established here, and independent reproduction remains open.
